prompt.v: Solve 2 cos x + 5 = 4 for −180° ≤ x < 360°. Give every solution in degrees.

problems.explain: Take away 5: 2 cos x = −1. Divide by 2: cos x = −1/2. The reference angle is 60°, since cos 60° = 1/2. Cosine is negative in quadrants II and III: x = 180° − 60° = 120° and x = 180° + 60° = 240°. Every solution is one of those plus a whole number of periods, 360° each: x = 120° + 360°k or x = 240° + 360°k. The ones from −180° up to 360° are −120°, 120° and 240°. (Negative angles count too: take a period away as well as adding one.) So x = −120° or x = 120° or x = 240°.

problems.explain: Divide by √2: sin(x/2) = −1/√2 = −√2/2. Let θ = x/2. As x runs from 0 to 2π, θ runs from 0 to π, half a turn. The reference angle is π/4, since sin π/4 = √2/2. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV: θ = π + π/4 = 5π/4 and θ = 2π − π/4 = 7π/4. Only those below π are in that half turn: θ = none. Multiply each by 2: x = none. (A θ past π gives an x past 2π, outside the interval.) So there is no solution.
